title: 1971 AHSME Problem 18
statement: The current in a river flows steadily at \(3\) miles per hour. A motorboat traveling at a constant rate in still water goes downstream \(4\) miles and then returns to its starting point. The trip takes one hour, excluding turning time. The ratio of the downstream rate to the upstream rate is:

solutions.text:
If \(v\) is the still-water speed, then \[ \frac4{v+3}+\frac4{v-3}=1. \] This simplifies to \(v^2-8v-9=0,\) so the positive admissible solution is \(v=9.\) The downstream and upstream rates are \(12\) and \(6,\) whose ratio is \(2:1.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(v\) be the boat’s still-water speed
